- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (≥ 5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for next 3–5 periods.  
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings, model tends to lag; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for next 3–5 periods to catch mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.10+), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before applying sentiment-adjusted correction.
